subject: [PATCH v3 3/4] mm: workingset: skip the root memcg flush in workingset_test_recent()

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the workingset_test_recent() function by skipping the root memory cgroup (memcg) flush when it's not necessary. The function now checks if the eviction memcg is the root memcg, and if so, reads the LRU sizes directly from the node counters instead of flushing the stats. This reduces the overhead of a root flush from 69us to ~150ns on an 80-CPU machine with little cgroup activity. The patch also keeps the flush for reclaim operations as it's still needed to keep up-to-date statistics.

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary: Recommended using a mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper to simplify the code and make it easier to understand. Acknowledged that skipping the root flush is acceptable, but suggested keeping the original patch's logic in mind for future changes.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Joanne Koong writes:
>-	if (flush)
>+	if (flush && !mem_cgroup_is_root(eviction_memcg))
> 		mem_cgroup_flush_stats_ratelimited(eviction_memcg);

Not a big deal, but in the v2 thread you mentioned you would try a
mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper for this, per Michal's
suggestion. That still seems like a good idea given this skip and the one in
DAMON rely on everything read after them staying in lruvec_use_node_stat(),
and at least speaking for myself, keeping the root check close to the list
in memcontrol.c makes that easier to see. It doesn't need
to hold this patch up though, and I've tested that refaults in the root
cgroup no longer flush, so either way:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

2026-11-16.patch_summary: The patch modifies the workingset_test_recent() function to skip flushing the root memcg's statistics when the eviction memcg is also the root memcg. This optimization avoids an expensive flush operation on the refault path, which can take up to 0.9ms in systems with high cgroup activity.
